evidence.text: Service: NEUROSURGERY
Allergies: Flecainide / Salmon
Headache
___ Resection of right occipital brain lesion

The pt is a ___ year old gentleman with atrial fibrillation s/p
cardioversion s/p PCI recently started on xarelto, AV block s/p
recent PPM ___, left temporal melanoma stage Ib s/p wide
resection in ___, hypertension, BPH, who presents for headache
x1 week, found on CT today to have a hyperdensity concerning for
hemorrhage in the right occipital lobe.
The patient was in his usual state of health until last
(9 days ago) when he woke up suddenly at 3am with a headache.

He
described it as sharp, "like a bombshell" which woke him up from
sleep.

Since then it has been persistent, with intermittent
flashes of worsening pain, but overall continuous sharp pain 
over
the right and at times left temporal region.

This worsens when 
he
lies down and is excruciating when he coughs.
He has been taking

Tylenol ___ q6h which provides some relief, but this only
lasts a few hours per dose.

Over the past week he also noted 
that
his balance was slightly off; he and his deny any listing toward
either side or falling, but he feels he needs to concentrate
harder in order to walk, which is unusual for him.

During one
walk with his wife and dog, he found that he could not see her 
as
well when she was in his left periphery.

He otherwise denies
blurred vision or double vision.

He was seen in his PCP's office earlier this week and was
prescribed fioricet, which he took with great relief, but again
the headache would return after 5 hours with the same intensity.

Today he returned to his PCP who was concerned given he had
recently been switched from aspirin 325mg to xarelto (one day
after headache onset), and ordered a noncontrast head CT.

This
showed a right parietal lobe hyperdensity concerning for
hemorrhage, and he was directed to the ED.

In ED, neurosurgery
was initially consulted and recommended a dose of dexamethasone
and keppra.

He was also ordered for transfusions of
cryoprecipitate and platelets but it does not appear he has
received them.

On neuro ROS, the pt denies loss of vision, blurred vision,
diplopia, dysarthria, dysphagia, lightheadedness, vertigo,
tinnitus or hearing difficulty.

Denies difficulties producing or
comprehending speech.

Denies focal weakness, numbness,
parasthesiae.

He endorses occasional bladder incontinence in
setting of his BPH, and at times needs to wear a pad when
traveling.
No bowel incontinence or retention.

On general review of systems, the pt denies recent fever or
chills.
No night sweats or recent weight loss or gain.

Denies
cough, shortness of breath.

Denies chest pain or tightness,
palpitations.

Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation 
or
abdominal pain.
No recent change in bowel or bladder habits.

No
dysuria.
Denies arthralgias or myalgias.
Denies rash.
Atrial fibrillation s/p cardioversion
Hypertension
Left temporal melanoma grade Ib s/p wide excision ___lock s/p PPM
No family history of cardiac disease.
=== ADMISSION EXAM ===
Vitals: temp 97.8 HR 70 BP 145/80 RR 18 spO2 97% RA
General: Awake, cooperative, NAD.
HEENT: NC/AT, no scleral icterus noted, MMM.
Neck: Supple, no nuchal rigidity
Pulmonary: Lungs CTA bilaterally
Cardiac: RRR, nl
Abdomen: soft, NT/ND
Extremities: No C/C/E bilaterally
Neurologic:
-Mental Status: Alert, oriented x3.

Able to relate history
without difficulty.

Attentive, able to name ___ backward without
difficulty.

Language is fluent with intact repetition and
comprehension.
Normal prosody.
There were no paraphasic errors.
Pt was able to name both high and low frequency objects.

Able 
to
read without difficulty.
Speech was not dysarthric.

Able to
follow both midline and appendicular commands.

Pt was able to
register 3 objects and recall ___ at 5 minutes.

There was no
evidence of apraxia or neglect.
-Cranial Nerves:
II, III, IV, VI: PERRL 3mm, minimally reactive, post-surgical
EOMI without nystagmus.
Normal saccades.

Homonymous left 
inferior
quadrantanopsia.

Fundoscopic exam revealed blurred disc margins
temporally without papilledema or hemorrhages.

Normal contoured
retinal vasculature.
V: Facial sensation intact to light touch.
VII: No facial droop, facial musculature symmetric.
VIII: Hearing intact to finger-rub bilaterally.
IX, X: Palate elevates symmetrically.
XI: ___ strength in trapezii and SCM bilaterally.
XII: Tongue protrudes in midline.
-Motor: Normal bulk, tone throughout.

No pronator drift
bilaterally.
No adventitious movements, such as tremor, noted.

No
asterixis noted.
Delt Bic Tri WrE FFl FE IO IP Quad Ham TA ___

-Sensory: Decreased sensation to vibration and proprioception in
the toes bilaterally.

Otherwise no deficits to light touch or
pinprick throughout.
-DTRs:
Bi Tri ___ Pat Ach
Plantar response was extensor bilaterally.
-Coordination: No intention tremor, no dysdiadochokinesia noted.
No dysmetria on FNF or HKS bilaterally.
-Gait: Difficulty with initiation, requires use of arms.

Able to
maintain standing position, without truncal ataxia.
Positive
Romberg.
Unable to tandem walk.
On Discharge:
Stable Neurological Exam
Incision closed with Sutures.
Pin site closed with Staples.

No 
erythema or drainage.
=== ADMISSION LABS ===
___ Abslymp: 1.96 Absmono: 0.70 Abseos: 0.20 Absbaso: 0.11
EKG: paced rhythm
=== IMAGING ===
CT Head WO Contrast ___.

Right parietal lobe hyperdensity indicative of lobar
hemorrhage, concerning for mass lesion with superimposed
hemorrhage.

CTA Head WWO Contrast ___.  20 x 23 mm right occipital hematoma with surrounding 
vasogenic edema and mild mass effect on adjacent sulci is 
overall unchanged compared to the prior examination.

No new 
hemorrhage.

2.  Unremarkable head CTA without evidence of stenosis, 
occlusion, or aneurysm formation.

No vascular abnormalities 
identified associated with the hematoma.

CT Abdomen & Pelvis WWO Contrast ___. 2 small hepatic hypodensities are incompletely characterized 
but likely 
cysts or biliary hamartomas.
2. No metastatic disease in the abdomen or pelvis.

This is a 
nonspecific finding, but given the patient's history of 
melanoma, could be compatible with a metastatic lesion.
Post Op NCHCT ___.

Expected postsurgical changes status post right occipital 
craniotomy with resection of intraparenchymal hemorrhage 
including pneumocephalus and edema at the surgical site.

There 
is a small amount of residual hemorrhage.

No significant mass 
effect or midline shift.
CT Head ___:

In comparison to the prior study from ___, there is a 
decreased 
amount of hyperdense material adjacent to the right occipital 
resection cavity (for example see series 4, image 18 for a small 
focus of residual blood products).

Pneumocephalus is persistent 
and minimally decreased in quantity along the right frontal 
convexity, with additional small foci seen adjacent to the 
resection cavity.

Regional white matter hypodensity adjacent to 
the resection cavity in the right occipital lobe is not 
appreciably changed.

There is no evidence of new focus of hemorrhage elsewhere, or CT 
evidence of superimposed acute large vascular territorial 
infarction.

Small hypodensity near the right putamen is 
unchanged, likely representing a dilated perivascular space or a 
chronic lacunar infarct.

There is preservation of gray-white 
matter differentiation.

The ventricles sulci are stable and 
normal in size and caliber.

There is no shift of normally 
midline structures.
The basal cisterns are patent.

Carotid 
siphon and distal vertebral artery calcifications are noted, 
unchanged.

There is minimal linear enhancement in the region surrounding 
the resection cavity.
No nodular enhancement.

No additional 
concerning foci of enhancement are seen elsewhere.

Right 
occipital calvarial defect in mild overlying scalp soft tissue 
irregularity is noted.
There is no evidence of fracture.

Skin 
staples are seen along the left temporoparietal region.

The 
visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear.
The globes, aside from bilateral lens removal, are unremarkable.
The bony orbits are intact.

___ year old gentleman with atrial fibrillation s/p cardioversion 
s/p PCI, recently started on Xarelto, AV block s/p recent PPM
___, left temporal melanoma stage Ib s/p wide resection in

___, hypertension, BPH; who presented with severe headache x1 
week.

CT found hyperdensity concerning for hemorrhage in the 
right parieto-occipital lobe.

His exam was significant for left 
inferior quadrantanopia.

CTA did not find vascular malformation 
but suggested possible malignancy.

The patient underwent a 
lesion resection with Dr. ___ on ___.

#Parietal lesion: Hemorrhagic in nature and suggestive of 
metastatic melanoma given his personal history.

Successful 
resection with Dr. ___ on ___.

The patient recovered well 
from the procedure with minimal pain management issues.

A 
frozen sample was inconclusive intraoperatively.

A CT with 
contrast was obtained post operatively in place of an MRI.

It 
revealed expected post operative changes with no new hemorrhage 
or residual nodular enhancement.

Repeat head CT on ___ was 
stable.

He will taper Dexamethasone to off over 5 days and 
continue on Keppra 1g BID for seizure prophylaxis.
#AV Block: s/p PPM insertion with Dr. ___ on ___.

The 
patient was intermittently A paced.

Given the recent nature of 
pacemaker insertion, he may not have an MRI for 6 weeks post 
procedure.

EP interrogated his pacemaker pre and 
postoperatively.

Please see their full consult note for 
details.

#Atrial arrhythmias: The patient has a history of atrial 
fibrillation and atrial flutter.

Intermittently and 
asymptomatically in 3:1 atrial flutter throughout admission.

He 
was previously on Xarelto for thromboembolic prophylaxis, which 
has been held throughout admission.
It can be restarted on
___, 1 week postoperatively.
#HTN: Well controlled during admission.

#BPH with Urinary Retention: The patient has a long standing 
history of urinary retention and had a foley inserted during 
admission.
He was evaluated by his home urologist.

On POD 2 the 
patient foley was removed and he was voiding independently with 
no residual.

At the time of discharge he is tolerating a regular diet, 
ambulating independently, afebrile with stable vital signs.
The Preadmission Medication list is accurate and complete.
1. Pravastatin 40 mg PO QPM
2. Lisinopril 20 mg PO DAILY
3. Rivaroxaban 20 mg PO QHS
4. Finasteride 5 mg PO DAILY
5. Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg PO DAILY
Mental Status: Clear and coherent.
Level of Consciousness: Alert and interactive.
Activity Status: Ambulatory - Independent.
1. Right parietal lobe hyperdensity indicative of lobar hemorrhage, concerning for mass lesion with superimposed hemorrhage.
1. 20 x 23 mm right occipital hematoma with surrounding vasogenic edema and mild mass effect on adjacent sulci is overall unchanged compared to the prior examination.
No new hemorrhage.
2. Unremarkable head CTA without evidence of stenosis, occlusion, or aneurysm formation.
No vascular abnormalities identified associated with the hematoma.
2.4 x 2.7 cm peripherally enhancing lesion in the region of previously identified intraparenchymal hemorrhage.
This is a nonspecific finding, but given the patient's history of melanoma, could be compatible with a metastatic lesion.
1. 2 small hepatic hypodensities are incompletely characterized but likely cysts or biliary hamartomas.
2. No metastatic disease in the abdomen or pelvis.
1. Mediastinal lymph nodes measuring up to 1.2 cm in short axis.
2. Evaluation of the lung parenchyma, especially in the right middle and bilateral lower lobes is severely restricted by motion artifact.
Within this limitation, there is a 10 mm nodule in the right middle lobe abutting the mediastinal pleura, unchanged in size since ___.
More linear opacities in the bilateral lower lobes, basal segments are likely subsegmental atelectasis.
1. No changes since ___ chest radiograph.
No consolidation, masses, nodules seen.
Dual chamber pacemaker in stable position.
Stable left ventricular hypertrophy.
1. Expected postsurgical changes status post right occipital craniotomy with resection of intraparenchymal hemorrhage including pneumocephalus and edema at the surgical site.
There is a small amount of residual hemorrhage.
No significant mass effect or midline shift.
Evolving postsurgical changes status post right occipital craniotomy and resection of mass, detailed above.
Small focus of residual blood products adjacent to the resection cavity site.
No new large focus of hemorrhage.
Aside from minimal linear enhancement at the resection cavity, there is no nodular enhancement, or abnormal focus of enhancement elsewhere.
Wound Care: 1 order(s) before T_pa; first on hospital day 7, most recent 40.8 h before T_pa.
Occupational Therapy, Physical Therapy: 4 order(s) before T_pa; first on hospital day 2, most recent 163.2 h before T_pa.
IV cefazolin: 1 order(s) running at some point in the 48 h before T_pa; stopped at T_pa; most recent start 34.1 h before T_pa.
